minutes.headline: Planning Board opened the marijuana bylaw hearing, approved the 400 Electric Ave site plan, and continued 190 Electric Ave.
minutes.summary: The board, short-handed, took public comment on a marijuana regulation article and six prohibition articles and continued that hearing to March 4. It continued the 190 Electric Ave solar hearing after revised tree-cutting plans, then approved the 400 Electric Ave site plan with conditions. It also discussed DLTA/walkability, MRPC, and the board's role in town building reuse.

Asked why the board would pass all seven articles at town meeting; discussed what setback distances mean on the ground.
Commended the board; raised typos and odor definition in the draft bylaw.
Objected to limiting retail marijuana stores to two as arbitrary.
Thanked the board for keeping prohibition open; supported limiting stores to two.
Said the revised 190 Electric Ave tree plan is fine with him.
Said his dealings with MRPC on bid results lacked transparency.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board approved the 400 Electric Avenue site plan with standard conditions, a Graves review letter and a sign note on the plan.
The board continued the marijuana regulation and prohibition articles hearing to March 4 after taking public comment on setbacks, odor wording and a limit on stores.
The 190 Electric Ave solar hearing was continued to March 4 after revised tree-cutting plans were presented.
The board appointed Paula Bertram to the open space ad hoc committee and tabled prior minutes for lack of eligible members.
The planner is to research DLTA state-funded walkability study options for the next meeting, and town building reuse is to go on a March agenda.

why_it_matters: The marijuana articles are still open, so the rules on store limits, setbacks and prohibition that go to Town Meeting can change before the board finishes its hearing.
A DLTA walkability study would use state-funded technical assistance rather than town money, so it may add no direct cost to the tax bill if the board pursues it.
watch_next: March 4 at 6:35 pm: continued hearings on the marijuana articles and on 190 Electric Ave.
The planner's DLTA and walkability options, due at the next meeting, and the town building reuse item on the March 4 or March 25 agenda.

reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the Bertram appointment, the tabled minutes, the 205 Sunset Lane ANR delay and the 400 Electric Avenue approval. They differ on the attendees and chair, on which votes are recorded, on whether the March 4 and March 25 dates were set, and on the $500 and $11 million figures that only we have. The biggest thing to check is that our minutes have the chair present and Mr. Walsh as a member, while the official minutes list the chair (Matthew Allison) as absent and Jeffrey Walsh as the Graves Engineering consultant.
